Tool 03

Graph Art

Your contribution graph is a 7-pixel-tall canvas. Paint on it, spell on it, export it.

BRUSH:

Click or drag to paint. 0 commits planned · busiest day needs 0 commits.

How the real thing works

Design your art

Plan the picture on a 7-row grid — one column per week. Letters and simple shapes read best; fine detail gets lost.

Generate the commit script

A small script walks the grid and creates backdated commits with GIT_AUTHOR_DATE set, stacking more commits on darker squares.

Push to a fresh repo

Push the script's output to a new public repository. GitHub counts the commits on your profile graph within a day or so.

Watch it render

Your profile graph redraws itself into the picture. Screenshot it before the year rolls over and it scrolls away.

FAQ

Does painting here change my real GitHub graph?
No. This is a drawing toy that runs entirely in your browser. The steps above describe how the real technique works if you want to do it for real.
Why 7 rows?
Because a week has 7 days. Each column of the contribution graph is one week, each cell is one day — so the canvas is always exactly 7 pixels tall.
How many commits does a dark square take?
GitHub shades squares relative to your busiest day. A common scheme is 1 / 3 / 6 / 10 commits for the four green levels, which is the scale this painter uses for its estimate.
Is graph art against the rules?
It's your own profile and your own commits. Plenty of developers do it openly — just don't be surprised when a recruiter asks why you committed 40 times on Christmas Day.

Field notes

From the notebook

Note 01 · The layout

Black first, cream after

The whole trick of this design is the hard cut: a black starfield hero, then everything else sits on cream paper with black borders and offset shadows. No gradients between worlds.

Note 02 · The mascot

One character, four poses

Atlas holding the page up, pointing at the videos, sitting in a star, and reclining over the footer wordmark. Same teal helmet, same purple suit — consistency is what makes it a mascot instead of clip art.

Note 03 · The secrets

Six things are hidden

The moon in the header is secret one of six. The footer keeps score. The rest are… around. Click things that look clickable. Type things that look typeable.
